mappings.note: Blood returns from the lungs to the heart through the pulmonary vein -- naming a vessel of the human transport pathway, C 3.2-LO-2.

Gas exchange in a woody stem happens through lenticels. Exchange of materials in a PLANT, so the competency C 3.2; LO-2 covers the human respiratory pathway only and C 4.2-LO-1 names only alveolus, nephron and villus.

The organelle that breaks down glucose for energy is the mitochondrion. C 3.1 names mitochondria among the cellular components; the question asks for the organelle, not the products, so not C 3.2-LO-3.
Plants absorb nitrogen as nitrates and nitrites -- raw-material sourcing for autotrophic nutrition, C 3.2-LO-1.
Villi help in absorption -- the villus is one of the three structures C 4.2-LO-1 relates to its function.
The final product of photosynthesis is glucose, stored as starch -- autotrophic nutrition, C 3.2-LO-1.
Lactic acid forms during vigorous exercise because oxygen supply falls short -- anaerobic respiration and its product, C 3.2-LO-3.
The contractile vacuole expels excess water and waste in a unicellular organism. Excretion outside the human body plan, so the competency C 3.2 rather than the human-only LO-2.
Which condition is not a circulatory disorder -- anchored on the human circulatory system, C 3.2-LO-2.
Xylem carries water and minerals from root to shoot -- C 4.3-LO-1.
A replanted seedling wilts because its root hairs are torn and water uptake into the xylem fails. Plant water transport, C 4.3-LO-1.
Which is NOT a purpose of transpiration -- tests the three real purposes against a distractor, all inside C 4.3-LO-1.
The rate oxygen moves from alveoli into blood -- alveolar structure (thin wall, short diffusion path) serving gas exchange, C 4.2-LO-1.
Glomerulus and Bowman's capsule filter the blood -- nephron structure serving its function, which is exactly what C 4.2-LO-1 asks for.
The kidney's structural AND functional unit is the nephron. The phrasing is itself the structure-to-function relation of C 4.2-LO-1, which is why it is preferred over the pathway outcome C 3.2-LO-2.
Human digestion starts in the mouth -- the first step of the nutrition sequence, C 3.2-LO-1.
Which reading indicates hypertension -- blood pressure in the human circulatory system, C 3.2-LO-2.
Flame cells are the excretory structures of flatworms. Excretion in a non-human animal, so the competency C 3.2, consistent with qid:104704.
Dialysis fluid matches plasma except that it carries no nitrogenous waste -- the human excretory pathway and what it removes, C 3.2-LO-2.
The main human excretory organ is the kidney -- naming the organ of the pathway, C 3.2-LO-2.
Alternate contraction and relaxation of the alimentary canal is peristalsis -- C 3.2-LO-1, as for qid:104691.
Breaking large fat droplets into small ones is emulsification -- a step of human digestion, C 3.2-LO-1.
Fat digestion ends in fatty acids and glycerol -- C 3.2-LO-1.
Blood gets from right ventricle to left ventricle only by way of the lungs -- the double-circulation pathway, C 3.2-LO-2.
Where digestion is extracellular -- distinguishes gut digestion from intracellular digestion in Amoeba. A nutrition-mode contrast, C 3.2-LO-1.
Photosynthesis as the anabolic process -- building complex molecules from simple ones is the autotrophic half of C 3.2-LO-1, in contrast to the catabolic respiration of C 3.2-LO-3.
What the human excretory system includes -- naming the organs of the pathway, C 3.2-LO-2.
Transport of soluble photosynthetic products is translocation -- phloem transport, C 4.3-LO-1.
Blood pressure is measured with a sphygmomanometer -- human circulation, C 3.2-LO-2.
What cells use ATP for. ATP is the form in which respiration's released energy is held, and 'the energy released' is the clause that distinguishes C 3.2-LO-3 from the other respiration codes.

MISFILED: this row and the run that follows it are Management of Natural Resources (NCERT ch.16) carrying a 'Life Processes' source tag. The purpose of rainwater harvesting is recharging groundwater -- the hydrosphere strand of C 2.8, the only competency in this frame about earth systems that support life. No LO exists under it.
Kulhs are the traditional canal system of Himachal Pradesh -- a water-harvesting structure, C 2.8.
The three R's (reduce, reuse, recycle) for conserving natural resources -- resource use within earth systems, C 2.8.

Amrita Devi Bishnoi died protecting the khejri trees. C 5.2 is the competency for a case study of Science in human life seen through Social Sciences and Ethics, and it names conservation of biodiversity explicitly -- a better fit than the ecological C 4.3 for a question about a person's act.
Khadins, bundhis, ahars and kattas are water-harvesting structures -- C 2.8, as for qid:104730.
The Tehri Dam is on the Bhagirathi/Ganga -- large dams as water management, C 2.8.
The Arabari forest was revived through A. K. Banerjee's work with local villagers -- a named case study of people and conservation, C 5.2 rather than the ecological C 4.3.
The Ganga Action Plan was launched to control river pollution -- water quality within earth systems, C 2.8.
The pH range freshwater life tolerates. Judged C 2.8 (hydrosphere and what supports life in it) rather than C 1.3: the question is about habitat quality, not about acid-base chemistry.
Definition of a natural resource -- the framing concept for the whole earth-systems competency, C 2.8.
Coliform bacteria in the Ganga come from untreated sewage -- water pollution, C 2.8.
Pick the combination containing no fossil fuel -- classifying energy resources, C 2.8.
Which activity is eco-friendly -- resource use and its effect on earth systems, C 2.8.
What a successful forest conservation strategy should involve -- the participation of local communities. That is the human and ethical dimension, C 5.2, not the ecological content of C 4.3.
The Arabari forest is dominated by sal. A question about the composition of a forest community, so the ecosystems competency C 4.3 rather than the people-and-ethics C 5.2 used for qid:104735.

Which are environment-friendly ('particle' is almost certainly a corruption of 'practices'; see the defect list). Option text is not stored, but the subject -- environmentally sound resource use -- is named in the stem, and C 2.8 is the only competency covering it.
Which of these is not a natural resource -- classification of resources, C 2.8.
Clearing forest for a single cultivated species promotes loss of biodiversity. A community- and ecosystem-level consequence, C 4.3.
STRANDED: this is a Life Processes question sitting inside the misfiled natural-resources run. The green colour of plants is chlorophyll in the chloroplast, one of the organelles named in C 3.1.
What conservation is -- managing natural resources so they persist, C 2.8.
What deforestation causes -- soil erosion and loss of species, an ecosystem-level consequence, so C 4.3 rather than the resource-classification code C 2.8.
The Chipko Andolan began in 1972 at Reni in Garhwal -- a named people-and-forests case study, C 5.2.
The three R's again -- duplicate of qid:104731 and mapped to the same code so the pair stays consistent.
What creates ecological imbalance in the biosphere -- interactions at the ecosystem and biome level, C 4.3.
Where major oil deposits are found -- distribution of a fossil-fuel resource in the geosphere, C 2.8.
The layer closest to the Earth's surface is the troposphere -- the atmosphere strand of C 2.8, which names atmosphere among the interconnected earth systems.
